notes: Tangent journeys. A tangent is a child session in this engine -- /tangent <name> switches onto one and bare /tangent returns to the parent -- so it belongs with the session journeys rather than with conversation history, and it shares the switch path that loading a session uses. What a user depends on is that the detour leaves no trace on the session they came back to, which is asserted from the transcript after the return.

scenarios.name: A tangent takes the session aside and returns it without the detour
scenarios.description: A turn on the root session, a named tangent with a turn of its own, then a return -- asserts the tangent is entered and marked, and that returning restores the root transcript without the tangent's turns
steps: prompt:this is the tangent turn TANGENTWORD-2
scenarios.observe: The tangent is entered by name and the run only proceeds once the session says so, so the detour is real rather than assumed. The return is the assertion that matters: the root answer is still there while the tangent's answer is not, which is what separates a session that came back from one that merely carried on. The tangent's own name is asserted absent too, because it labels the status bar while the detour is active and a return that left the label would leave the user unsure which session they are on.

scenarios.name: The tangent list states the absence, then shows the tree once one exists
scenarios.description: A tangent listing before any tangent exists and again after creating one -- asserts the empty case is stated rather than blank, and the populated case shows the tangent under its root with the current one marked
scenarios.observe: The empty listing is taken first and acts as the control: the same command, before any tangent exists, states the absence rather than opening an empty picker. After creating one the listing is a tree -- the tangent under its root -- with the active one marked, which is what tells a user where they are once several exist. The switch affordance is asserted because a list of tangents you cannot move between is only half the surface.

scenarios.name: The bare tangent command starts a named detour when there is none to leave
scenarios.description: The tangent command with no argument, issued on the root session -- asserts it opens an auto-named tangent and marks it, which is the opposite of what the same command does while already on one
scenarios.observe: The same bare command does opposite things depending on where it is issued: on a tangent it returns to the parent, and on root it opens a new one under an auto-assigned name. Pinning the root case is what keeps that asymmetry deliberate -- a change that made it a no-op at root, or that reused the command only for returning, would fail here while the return journey still passed. The root answer is asserted still present because opening a detour must not disturb what it branched from, and the go-back hint because it is how a user learns the command's other meaning.
